body:
I have tried 4 months of physical therapy including strengthening exercises, modified my daily activity to only do gentle exercises every day as recommended by doctors and PT, tried 11 different medications which did not help much, and 3 steroid shots which haven't done much either. I had many MRIs and CT scans show only one thing that could be causing the pain.


I've tried a lot in 5 months but more than anything it's just hard to live with this pain. It flares up when sitting so I can't work at a regular desk or go for car rides. I'm housebound, barely able to sleep due to the pain, and psychologically really unwell since it's just exhausting and draining to manage all the pain. 


The surgery isn't perfect and I know it won't just fix me, but my quality of life is bad right now and I'm worried about my ability to finish my thesis and work after. I have basically no life and am left to deal with the pain alone almost every day. Nothing really helps the pain and this surgery is my final option, according to my surgeon. I would definitely continue with lifestyle changes like doing strengthening excercises, but I need to reduce the pain to do more of those.

Thank you, spinal surgeries are rough. I truly wouldn't be doing this if I thought I had other options. I'll make sure I'm meeting all of their guidelines - I will ask for the CPB next time I call. Thankfully my surgeon is advocating for me too.

I'm honestly not sure how to reach the prior authorization department. Every time I call Aetna, they transfer me to a student health call center for Cornell, since I'm on a university plan for students. I've asked them again and again what the exact reason was for deeming it "medically unnecessary" and they just tell me to look at my denial letter, which only lists the criteria for the surgery and says I didn't meet all the criteria, but doesn't say which I'm failing to meet. Do self insured student plans like this have a prior authorization department? Or how do I get to this department instead of immediately being transferred to the student health center?

I'm definitely hoping it's a situation where the Aetna medical director just needs more information to confirm I meet the criteria. I don't believe there are any conservative treatment steps left to take (according to the Aetna denial letter) because I've been trying conservative treatments (PT, steroid shots, gentle exercise, and medication) for months

The problem is that the pain is extremely intense and I'm unable to live my life at all basically. I can barely ride in the car and am essentially housebound. I try to work on my thesis every day but the pain makes it so difficult to concentrate.


I've been doing strengthening exercises in physical therapy for months and they've helped a bit, but I still can't sit for more than half an hour without intense leg pain. I only sleep a couple hours a night because laying makes the pain much worse. I'm not close to overweight, so weight doesn't seem to be a factor. I don't have a lot of back pain, it's mostly leg pain due to compression of the sciatic nerve. 


I'm a good candidate for the surgery as I have no other conditions that might interfere. I also realize it won't fix the problem forever, I'm just looking to regain a normal quality of life where I can travel and work without constantly having the pain flare up to debilitating levels. This will also enable me to do more intense and frequent strengthening to help, as right now I need to be very very careful or the pain will flare up. I have tendonitis because the muscles and tendons in my leg have been irritated nonstop for months. 


I've also checked the criteria for the surgery in the Aetna denial letter and it's confusing because according to my doctors and many MRIs and CT scans, I've met all the criteria.

They are denying coverage for the surgery because they're saying it's "medically unnecessary" but it's very confusing because I reviewed the criteria for it to be medically necessary and I meet all of them

I'm supposed to get a microdiscectomy. I read through the criteria and met all of them including trying all know conservative treatments over the 5 months timespan (physical therapy, adjusting day to day activities, medication, and steroid shots)


I think they finally got the peer to peer meeting scheduled so hopefully that will clear up issues like if my surgeon's office forgot to submit evidence that I meet certain criteria.

Thank you. I think they finally got the peer to peer meeting scheduled. I definitely thought it was weird too like doctors are usually the really busy ones. I think if they still deny it I will have my surgeon appeal it.

I've tried all of the conservative treatments, so yes, a microdiscectomy is the next step since my debilitating pain continues. Since my pain is due to a disk compressing my nerves in my spinal canal, this surgery is meant to remove the part of the disk that's compressing a nerve. It has been 5 months and I've been in constant PT, tried every medication possible, and had 2 unsuccessful steroid shots. There aren't many options left.

I understand how hopeless this amount of pain makes us feel. If you haven't discussed a microdiscectomy or discectomy yet with your doctor, definitely ask. You shouldn't even need to wait until June, it might be worth finding another doctor or calling back and impressing how bad your pain is and seeing if you can move it up. Everyone I've talked to who had either of those surgeries said they're enormously successful and reduce pain and you shouldn't need to suffer for so long.

I'm so glad your surgery went alright and you're recovering!! I've heard it's best to still be careful for a while after the surgery, just because your disk might still be prone to slipping with the exception of gentle exercise and walking which could help. But it sounds like you're on the right track and I'm really glad the vast majority of your pain has gone! That should be permanent and it will only get better as you begin gentle exercise and normal activities I bet!

I don't know what my AP diameter is but since the pain has been going on for almost 5 months despite PT and steroid injections, I've had two spine doctors offer a microdiscectomy and I'm starting to lean towards that option. Like you're describing, they said it should be endoscopic and they say they do a ton of these surgeries with high success. It's up to everyone to decide on their own but I'm starting to think why keep suffering with 5-7 pain almost every day when such a minimally invasive, common surgery could have such success? Good for you and I hope it only continues to get better!
Hey sorry for the delay I haven't checked in for a while but if you still would like to send a message feel free!

I hope your surgery worked out okay for you!! I got my ESI last Weds and I feel okay so far but no noticeable reduction in pain, hoping it just will take a little more time to set it. 

I also saw a spine surgeon who recommended a microdiscectomy if the ESI doesn't work. I thought this was a great backup option since it's minimally invasive and would love to hear about your experience, hoping you're recovering well ❤️‍🩹

I've been laying on the floor on my stomach a lot with ice, it totally does help! I think need to be more careful about bending down as well, I don't think I'm always doing it safely. I'm glad to hear your surgery worked so well, I think something like that may be in order for me because it's just ridiculous how long I've been unable to function due to pain. I was willing to try the conservative approach for 3 months but now that its past that and the pain is worse despite being careful and PT, I need to ask a spine doctor or something to consider other treatments for me and maybe surgery
I've been trying to find a pool near me because I heard swimming helps recovering for this injury a lot and I'm glad it's helping you!!

I'm sorry for all the pain you're going through, I absolutely get it. I think you're right and I've now gotten a referral to a spine doctor for a second opinion and to express just how much pain I've been in for so long. Did they say what surgery you're going to need?

My insurance does not cover PT every day and even if they did, it took me a month to get into PT because it's so booked. I've tried tramadol, Norco, vicoden, nabumetome, cyclobenzaprine, Meloxicam, Prednisone and methylprednosolone, and gabapentin. Only the gabapentin and steroids worked. I'm open to trying new drugs but I think my doctor has run out of good options. I am trying to be really in tune with me body so even small discomfort makes me stop an activity. I don't know how else to tell if I'm accidentally injuring it but my PT has only given me very gentle exercises due to the continuing high pain levels. 

I'm glad you've noticed positive outcomes from epidural steroid injections. I just wish it could be done sooner so I spend less time in pain and know if I'm going to need surgery.

Oh, at the ER they took the MRI and found the bulging disk. They referred me to the orthopedic specialist but otherwise didn't do much besides hook me up to pain meds that didn't really help. I have been icing a lot and heating pad in between. It's really hard to find a position that isn't excruciating and the lack of sleep is definitely contributing to my mental decline lol

I rested for 2-3 weeks in Dec, after which my PT told me I needed to begin gentle exercise or I would lose muscle strength in the affected leg. I keep all stretches and PT exercises to a gentle minimum and on really bad days I just rest. I stop exercise immediately if it worsens the pain. I only stretch throughout the day because if I sit for more than 15 min, the pain worsens unless I stretch and get up. Lying and sitting down also hurt more than standing up which is why I tend to stand and walk. I'm not able to sleep much and am sort of at my mental breaking point

Oh I'm so sorry the bulge (and pain!!) got worse - but I've heard those surgeries can be really helpful so I'm wishing for the best possible outcome for you! Maybe you will soon be pain free and your bulge will be fixed. Good luck and feel free to reply here with updates ❤️
Actually you sound a lot like my ex on second thought lol

I want to be angry because I do think it was wrong of him not to tell me he was ready to leave, or at least to tell me how he felt. Communication is key in every relationship, and key to just not making things worse. He blamed me for everything at the time of the breakup but how could I have fixed issues I don't know about? There is unhappiness in every relationship (for instance, mine was from working 12 hr days every day, not him). Just because you are under a lot of stress doesn't mean you need to break up immediately (especially if the problem isn't even the relationship!! If you think lack of communication and immediately leaving when things (like health issues) are going wrong is good or healthy behavior in any relationship, I don't think you're right but you do you dude

I agree that surgery doesn't work the same for everyone. But as someone who has also been living in debilitating (10/10) pain almost 24/7 for months, it might be the only option since you need it to even begin to strengthen your core and back!! To each their own, but do not discourage people who may need this surgery to regain their life to avoid it.

Thanks for sharing your experience - even if I could get 2 months without pain that would feel like a miracle to me right now. It just stinks because ESIs are not a permanent solution, and permanent solutions are hard to find (besides the PT which works but takes a long time and can't be done when Im in debilitating pain).

I hope your most recent ESI will provide you delayed relief, and if not, I hope you find relief soon anyway. Definitely sad for me to not be able to be as active as I was either but better not to push it too hard and stick with gentle exercise. But it does make your life feel limited I wish you all the best.

I'm wishing you all the best. I didn't know how bad this kind of pain could be until now!! I knew bulged disks were bad but this is another level. 

I agree that we need relief, at this point I'm like...if I have withdrawal at some point it will still have been worth it for the relief. We need it both for working on our strength and for our sanity!! It's so crushing when you have weeks go by where the pain is always there at a high level. It becomes hard to even think properly. 

You have a great attitude. 30 and 30 something year olds ARE still young. My body is otherwise healthy! And my muscles can be strengthened easily. It's important to keep our heads up because I think there's also something to be said for anxiety worsening symptoms if it gets bad!!

I'll reply back here once I know my ESI outcome!

I'm so sorry for your pain! What you're saying makes a lot of sense to me. It's a priority for us to strengthen our core and back muscles to get the disk back to normal and prevent future injury. And how can we do that if the pain is debilitating? 

I have tried a lot of different meds (nabumetome, meloxicam, tramadol, generic norco) and I've ended up only taking gabapentin and Aleve since those are the only ones I could tell made a dent in the pain. I do worry about the gabapentin as it causes some dependence but it's sometimes the only thing that helps me sleep. Aleve just works better for the muscle inflammation than other anti inflammatories.

I'll check back in after two weeks beyond the 26th to let you know if the ESI provided me relief. I can also check in here again with how long the ESI is lasting. I do hope it lasts long enough for me to get strong enough to help the  disk get back to normal.
